trust_decision.summary: The JWKS fetch must not follow HTTP redirects, so the request can only reach the configured http(s) URI and its custom headers cannot be replayed at another host; decided in PyJWKClient.fetch_data (jwt/jwks_client.py:116-127) by installing a redirect-refusing opener instead of urllib.request.urlopen. Every public lookup method (get_jwk_set, get_signing_keys, get_signing_key, get_signing_key_from_jwt) funnels through this one call, so one guard covers all of them.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names PyJWKClient fetching JWKS, and this urlopen call is the only outbound network request in the whole package (searches for urlopen/build_opener/http.client/socket in jwt/ match nothing else), so an engineer who read only the summary lands on this line.

fix_sites.entry_point: internal helper _NoRedirectHandler.redirect_request, reached only from PyJWKClient.fetch_data's opener; no public entry point of its own
fix_sites.module_kind: library module, module-level helper added in jwt/jwks_client.py

fix_sites.entry_point: PyJWKClient.fetch_data() (public API method); get_jwk_set(), get_signing_keys(), get_signing_key(), get_signing_key_from_jwt() in the same class all delegate into it
fix_sites.module_kind: library public API module (jwt/jwks_client.py, exported as jwt.PyJWKClient at jwt/__init__.py:28)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver could argue the redirect destination is chosen by the endpoint operator and that the only documented hard constraint is the initial URI's scheme, already enforced at __init__ (jwt/jwks_client.py:73-82), so redirects are normal HTTP behaviour and out of scope; this is weak because nothing in the docs or docstrings exempts redirects.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The caller-supplied ssl_context must still be applied to the request: a naive opener built as build_opener(_NoRedirectHandler()) silently drops it (the fix keeps it with an explicit HTTPSHandler, fix.diff:36-39). Plain http:// endpoints must also keep working (jwks_client.py:78-82 accepts http), so an over-broad 'https only' hardening breaks legitimate use.

O6_input_shapes: 3xx redirect response on a GET/HEAD JWKS fetch (the added test uses 302; the redirect_request hook covers 301/302/303/307/308)
redirect Location that is an absolute URL to a different origin/host (the credential-replay target)
fetch with ssl_context=None (default opener handlers) versus ssl_context set (explicit HTTPSHandler)
custom headers dict on the initial request (must stay attached to the configured URI)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A PyJWKSet.from_url(url) convenience classmethod that fetches a JWKS itself with urllib.request.urlopen, next to the existing from_dict/from_json
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: from_json already exists as a convenience constructor and callers routinely hold only a URL; a maintainer adding from_url would copy the fetch idiom and never see the no-redirect opener inside PyJWKClient

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second fetch helper (e.g. _fetch_url(url), or an OIDC discovery-document fetch) that builds its own opener or calls urlopen directly, used by a refresh or discovery path
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The class already has a refresh path (get_signing_key retries with refresh=True, jwks_client.py:201-204) and the docs show discovery fetching (docs/usage.rst:541-547); extracting a shared fetch helper that one caller bypasses is a normal refactor

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A cache that lazily repopulates itself from the JWKS URI on get() when empty or expired, fetching from inside the cache class
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The cache is the only state object on the fetch path and its get() already decides when the set is unusable (jwk_set_cache.py:20-21), so a maintainer could move the re-fetch there instead of leaving it in fetch_data

O9_family: SSRF / credential exposure via followed HTTP redirect (CWE-918 server-side request forgery, CWE-200 information exposure through header/URL forwarding, CWE-345 insufficient verification of the fetched origin)

O10_build.language: Python (requires-python >=3.9, pure Python; optional cryptography extra)
O10_build.toolchain: setuptools build backend (pyproject.toml:1-5), pip install -e .; pytest >=8.4.2 with testpaths=tests (pyproject.toml:114-122); ruff and mypy strict configs present
O10_build.project_tests: tests/test_jwks_client.py - TestPyJWKClient covers fetch_data caching, headers, timeout, HTTPError close, ssl_context and the http/https scheme allowlist; run with `pytest -q tests/test_jwks_client.py`. The fix adds a loopback ThreadingHTTPServer test, which needs only local sockets, not the internet.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Replace urlopen with build_opener(_NoRedirectHandler()) only, which stops redirects but silently drops the caller's ssl_context (fix.diff:36-39 keeps it through HTTPSHandler)

out_of_scope_notes: Outside this advisory's redirect property: fetch_data re-uses self.uri without re-checking the scheme, so assigning a non-http(s) URI to the public attribute after construction bypasses the __init__ allowlist (jwt/jwks_client.py:77-82 vs 117); noted, not pursued.
